R0043.title: Stolen Card Payment
R0043.definition: Using the identity from a stolen payment card or another user's account to complete transactions.
R0043.description: Using the identity from a stolen payment card or another user's account to complete transactions. This is generally used to conceal the attacker's identity or reduce the risk of bulk order fraud being intercepted by risk controls. Login credentials come from carding attacks (R0040), and payment information comes from card cracking (R0041).

references.title: Ping An Bank Credit Card Strengthens Tech Empowerment, 'Black Hawk Eye' Deters Financial Black-Grey Market

observables: The payment card BIN used at checkout differs significantly from the account's historically common cards and originates from a known leaked BIN range
The account jumps to payment immediately after login, and the payment card information does not match the account's verified identity
The same payment card is used alternately across orders placed by multiple different accounts
The order placement device environment shows cross-border or cross-region contradictions with the card's issuing country and the shipping address
The device fingerprint and IP of payment requests deviate significantly from the account's historical environment, accompanied by bulk ordering characteristics

R0043-001.title: Stolen Card Fraud
R0043-001.definition: Using funds from a stolen payment card or another user's account to purchase goods or cash out.
R0043-001.description: Using stolen payment card or account login credentials and payment information to misappropriate or steal funds. In addition to conventional purchases/services/withdrawals, profits can also be made through refunds. Login credentials come from carding attacks (R0040), and payment information comes from card cracking (R0041).
R0043-001.influence: Funds in the payment card or account are misappropriated or stolen.

references.title: OWASP Automated Threat: OAT012 Cashing Out

observables: After a remote or new-device login, the account initiates withdrawals, transfers, or large purchases within a short window
Payment card funds are quickly spent and then flow back for cash-out via refunds or returns
The same stolen card or account places rapid orders across multiple merchants with amounts close to the available balance limit
The shipping address for orders is a new address or significantly different from the account's historical addresses
The device environment for withdrawal or transfer requests is inconsistent with the account's historical environment, accompanied by risk-control evasion characteristics
